dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 12.2-day, ~2.9-hour flat-bottom dip repeating steadily over three transits with no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse and consistent depths, best explained as a ~5-6 Earth-radius planet transiting an M dwarf. The dip is on the target and large enough that a background binary would be detectable. The low signal-to-noise and only three events and Gaia suggesting a larger stellar radius remain to be checked with more photometry.
